expectations.name: 01-raises-the-incident
expectations.text:
The agent's last message raises the earlier incident: in 2024 retries that drew a fresh idempotency key charged
members twice, which is why every attempt sends the same key.
expectations.evidence: “reusing the same idempotency key across retries of one capture is intentional ... a 2024 incident where each retry drew a fresh key caused 41 members to be double-charged.” It also explains that a gateway timeout after charging followed by a retry with a new key charges the card again.

expectations.name: 02-read-the-owning-page
expectations.text: The agent reads docs/features/payments.md before its first edit.
expectations.evidence: first read of docs/features/payments.md at step 9; first edit at step None

expectations.name: 03-acts-on-the-incident
expectations.text:
The agent acts on the earlier incident: it leaves the change out and says why, asks first, or makes it while warning, in
its message, the code or the docs, that it brings back members charged twice when a timed-out attempt had already
charged the card, as in 2024.
expectations.evidence: The agent leaves the change out and explains: "Giving each retry attempt its own idempotency key would reintroduce that exact double-charge risk: if the gateway times out *after* actually charging the card, a retry with a new key charges it again." It explicitly connects this to the 2024 incident that double-charged 41 members.
